question: Two trains of lengths 160 m and 90 m are running in the same direction with velocities of 40 km/h and 50 km/h, respectively. The time taken by them to cross each other is:
solution:
Given:

Length of the 1st train = 160m

Length of the 1st train = 90m

speeds are 40 km/h and 50 km/h.

Concept used:

Relative speed = speed of 1st train - speed of 2nd train; when both are moving in the same direction

Time = distance/speed

Calculation:

Relative speed = 50 - 40 = 10 km/hr

Total distance = 160 + 90

We know that, 

Time = distance/speed

⇒ T = (250/10) × 18/5

⇒ T = 90sec

∴ Time taken is 90 second.
